title: What is ATS? How Nigerian Companies Screen Your CV in 2024
excerpt: Learn how ATS systems work in Nigerian companies like GTBank, MTN, and Dangote. Discover how to optimize your CV to pass automated screening.
author: ElevateResume

body.text: If you've ever wondered why your perfectly crafted CV seems to disappear into a black hole after applying to major Nigerian companies like First Bank, Dangote Group, or MTN, you're likely encountering an Applicant Tracking System (ATS). Understanding how these systems work is crucial for Nigerian job seekers in today's competitive market.
What is an Applicant Tracking System (ATS)?

An Applicant Tracking System is software that helps companies manage their recruitment process by automatically screening, sorting, and ranking CVs before human recruiters ever see them. Think of it as a digital gatekeeper that decides whether your application makes it to the hiring manager's desk.

In Nigeria, over 70% of large corporations and multinational companies now use ATS software to handle the thousands of applications they receive daily. Companies like Zenith Bank, Shell Nigeria, Unilever Nigeria, and consulting firms like PwC Nigeria rely heavily on these systems to streamline their hiring processes.
The ATS acts as the first filter in your job application journey. If your CV isn't optimized for these systems, it may never reach human eyes, regardless of how qualified you are.
How ATS Works: The Technical Process
When you submit your CV through a company's career portal or job boards like Jobberman, MyJobMag, or LinkedIn, here's what happens:
1. Document Parsing

The ATS scans your CV and extracts information like your contact details, work experience, education, and skills. It then organizes this data into a standardized format that recruiters can easily review.
2. Keyword Matching

The system searches for specific keywords and phrases that match the job description. For instance, if you're applying for a digital marketing role at a Lagos-based fintech company, the ATS might look for terms like "social media marketing," "Google Analytics," "campaign management," and "content creation."
3. Ranking and Scoring
Based on keyword matches, relevant experience, and other criteria, the ATS assigns a score to your application. CVs with higher scores are prioritized and shown to recruiters first.
4. Database Storage
Your information is stored in the company's candidate database, which recruiters can search when new positions become available.

body.text: Why Nigerian Companies Use ATS
Volume Management
A single job posting by companies like GTBank or Nestle Nigeria can attract thousands of applications. Manual screening would be impossible and extremely time-consuming.
Consistency in Screening
ATS ensures that every application is evaluated using the same criteria, reducing human bias and improving fairness in the initial screening process.
Cost Efficiency
Automated screening significantly reduces the time HR teams spend on initial CV reviews, allowing them to focus on interviewing qualified candidates.
Compliance and Record-Keeping
ATS helps companies maintain detailed records of their hiring processes, which is particularly important for multinational corporations operating in Nigeria.

Common ATS Mistakes That Kill Nigerian CVs
Using Creative Formats
While a beautifully designed CV might impress human recruiters, ATS systems struggle with:

items: Headers and footers containing crucial information

body.text: Incorrect File Types
Some ATS systems have trouble with PDF files created by certain design software. Always save your CV as a standard Word document (.docx) or a simple PDF when applying through ATS portals.
Missing Keywords

Failing to include relevant keywords from the job description is the biggest mistake Nigerian job seekers make. If the job posting mentions "project management," but you only write "managed projects," the ATS might not make the connection.
Inconsistent Formatting
Using different date formats (DD/MM/YYYY vs MM/DD/YYYY) or inconsistent job title formatting can confuse ATS systems.
Always tailor your CV keywords to match each specific job application. What works for a banking role at First Bank won't necessarily work for a consulting position at McKinsey Nigeria.

Testing Your CV Against ATS
Before submitting applications, test your CV using these methods:
Copy-Paste Test
Copy your CV content and paste it into a plain text document. If the formatting looks jumbled or information is missing, an ATS might have similar issues.
Keyword Density Check
Ensure you've included relevant keywords from the job description at least 2-3 times throughout your CV, but avoid keyword stuffing.
Online ATS Simulators
Several websites offer ATS compatibility checks. While not perfect, they can highlight potential issues with your CV format.

Conclusion

Understanding ATS systems is no longer optional for Nigerian job seekers—it's essential. By optimizing your CV for these automated systems while maintaining its appeal to human recruiters, you significantly increase your chances of landing interviews at top Nigerian companies.

Remember, the goal isn't to game the system but to present your qualifications in a format that both ATS software and human recruiters can easily understand and appreciate. With the right approach, you can navigate the digital gatekeepers and showcase your talents to the employers who matter most.
Keep your ATS-optimized CV updated regularly. As you gain new skills and experiences, ensure they're reflected using current industry keywords that Nigerian employers are searching for.
